title: What should a dial on the training workbench sound like when she turns it?
question: The training workbench's dials plate (design/14) landed with no sound on a turn — pressing a dial's minus or plus, or holding its picture to reset it, is silent. Three CC0 recordings from Freesound clear the bar for a short, dry, mechanical click: pick the one that plays, or say none of them do.
why_now: The workbench is built for v0.2.2 with this one gap; you asked for it filled today, free-to-use first, the same way the harvest sound was found.

options.label: "dial turn" — freemaster2 (Recommended)
options.detail: Freesound #120844, CC0 1.0. 0.13s, all click, no tail — the whole file is the hit. The title also says what it is. Wired in now as the game's `dial` sound.

options.label: "Switch Klunk 2" — cookies+policy
options.detail: Freesound #556634, CC0 1.0. A two-part click-then-thunk in its first 0.2s (the file runs to 1.09s but the rest is silence the fetch tool kept rather than trimmed). Heavier than (a) — reads more like a latch settling than a dial clicking.

options.label: "Metronome click 2" — Sadiquecat
options.detail: Freesound #793345, CC0 1.0. An 11ms tick with a fast decay (the file runs to 0.62s, again mostly trailing silence). Cleaner and higher-pitched than (a) — closer to a UI tick than a mechanical turn.

options.label: None of these — keep looking, or record one
options.detail: Sends the audio designer back to Freesound with different search terms, or — if nothing free lands — onto the foley list for the next recording session, batched with whatever else is waiting on it by then.

ruled.summary: "dial turn" by freemaster2 stays as the dial's sound; the other two candidates stay in the credits, unwired.
